title: M08. Circuit-linear communication with only one honest participant
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Obtain constant-round malicious MPC tolerating \(n-1\) corruptions with communication \(O(|C|\operatorname{poly}(\lambda))+\operatorname{poly}(n,\lambda)\), using weak assumptions such as ordinary OT and avoiding stronger general-purpose primitives.
status: Current round-collapse results require a constant honest fraction. A 2024 DDH construction tolerates \(n-1\) corruptions but retains an \(O(|C|n)\) circuit term.
why: Would determine whether almost-total collusion inherently imposes per-gate communication proportional to party count.
key_works: Goyal et al. (2024), [*Dishonest Majority Constant-Round MPC with Linear Communication from DDH*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1466); Goyal–Li–Ostrovsky–Song (2025/2026), [*Towards Building Scalable Constant-Round MPC from Minimal Assumptions via Round Collapsing*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/508).

title: M09. Adaptivity-preserving compression of MPC rounds
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Develop a round-compression theorem preserving erasure-free adaptive security and near-linear circuit communication, with explicit security loss depending on corruption timing and count.
status: Proposed compiler target. Existing round-collapse results do not establish this complete combination.
why: Participants can be compromised during a long computation; static security does not cover that threat.
key_works: Goyal–Li–Ostrovsky–Song (2025/2026), [*Towards Building Scalable Constant-Round MPC from Minimal Assumptions via Round Collapsing*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/508); Canetti et al. (2002), [*Universally Composable Two-Party and Multi-Party Secure Computation*](https://doi.org/10.1145/509907.509980).

title: M10. Efficient guaranteed output delivery from OWFs without random oracles
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Match constant-round honest-majority MPC with guaranteed output delivery and circuit-linear-in-\(n\) communication using ordinary OWFs in the standard model.
status: Li–Song’s 2026 protocol achieves the relevant combination in the random-oracle model, with communication \(O(|C|n\lambda+Dn^3\lambda^3+W_I\operatorname{poly}(n,\lambda))\).
why: Would place low-latency, availability-preserving MPC on an explicit minimal assumption.
key_works: Li–Song (2026), [*Achieving Guaranteed Output Delivery MPC with Constant Rounds and Linear Communication in Minicrypt*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1296).

title: M11. Guaranteed output delivery without the depth surcharge
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Eliminate the \(Dn^3\lambda^3\) communication term in constant-round honest-majority MPC with guaranteed output delivery, or prove a matching depth-dependent lower bound.
status: The September 2026 Li–Song revision retains this surcharge despite achieving constant rounds.
why: Deep computations otherwise pay a substantial extra communication cost for guaranteed completion.
key_works: Li–Song (2026), [*Achieving Guaranteed Output Delivery MPC with Constant Rounds and Linear Communication in Minicrypt*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1296).

title: M12. Network-agnostic MPC with near-quadratic setup
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Reduce the circuit-independent overhead of perfectly secure network-agnostic MPC to \(\widetilde O(n^2)\), preserving polynomial computation and optimal synchronous/asynchronous corruption thresholds.
status: Ji–Liu-Zhang–Song’s October 2026 revision achieves \(O((|C|n+(D+C_I)n^2+n^6)\log n)\) bits under the optimal threshold \(n>2\max(t_s,t_a)+\max(2t_a,t_s)\).
why: Would remove an enormous startup cost from protocols designed for uncertain network timing.
key_works: Ji–Liu-Zhang–Song (2026), [*Perfectly Secure Network-Agnostic MPC Comes for Free*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/377).

title: M13. Responsive network-agnostic secure computation
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Combine optimal network-agnostic resilience and perfect privacy with latency tracking actual message delays during fast executions, while retaining security under arbitrary delays.
status: Proposed strengthening of the 2026 feasibility theorem. Responsiveness must cover preprocessing, evaluation, and reconstruction separately.
why: Applications could benefit from fast networks without trusting them to remain fast.
key_works: Ji–Liu-Zhang–Song (2026), [*Perfectly Secure Network-Agnostic MPC Comes for Free*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/377).

title: M14. Asynchronous weighted and fluid MPC
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Construct maliciously secure MPC with changing weighted membership and guaranteed output delivery in asynchronous networks, characterizing the required honest-weight overlap between successive committees.
status: Almashaqbeh–Ghude’s 2026 work combines weighted participation, dynamic membership, and guaranteed delivery under synchrony.
why: Long-running computations often involve organizations with unequal trust, resources, and availability.
key_works: Almashaqbeh–Ghude (2026), [*MPC with Weighted and Fluid Participation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1375).

title: M15. Near-linear private-state handover between weighted committees
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Transfer an \(S\)-element private MPC state using \(O(S+n\operatorname{poly}(\lambda))\) field elements, with malicious security and proactive refresh under a fixed positive honest-weight margin.
status: Proposed efficiency target beyond the 2026 feasibility results for weighted proactive sharing and state handover.
why: Would make committee rotation affordable for large persistent private states.
key_works: Almashaqbeh–Ghude (2026), [*MPC with Weighted and Fluid Participation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1375).

title: M16. Asynchronous MPC within tenfold synchronous throughput overhead
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Demonstrate asynchronous MPC with guaranteed delivery at \(t<n/3\), within \(10\times\) the throughput cost of a matched synchronous implementation for \(n=32,64,128\), including preprocessing and adversarial delays.
status: Proposed moonshot benchmark. Linear-amortized-communication theory and RondoMPC’s practical preprocessing improvements establish relevant starting points.
why: Would quantify—and potentially sharply reduce—the practical cost of removing synchrony assumptions.
key_works: Goyal–Liu-Zhang–Song (2024), [*Towards Achieving Asynchronous MPC with Linear Communication and Optimal Resilience*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/243); Meng et al. (2026), [*RondoMPC*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1261).

title: M17. Communication-optimal asynchronous identifiable abort
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Determine tight communication and latency bounds for asynchronous MPC with identifiable abort under the relaxed correctness and input-loss definitions permitting improved corruption thresholds.
status: Appan–Heath–Ren’s 2026 work establishes feasibility boundaries; the quantitative frontier remains open.
why: Applications need to understand the precise cost of accountability when guaranteed completion is unavailable.
key_works: Appan–Heath–Ren (2026), [*Asynchronous MPC with Abort*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/455).

title: M18. Low-overhead protection against super-rushing
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Compile synchronous malicious MPC into protocols tolerating adversaries that observe some next-round messages before fixing all current-round messages, preserving resilience and near-linear communication. The compiled protocol must permit event-driven advancement without restoring round-end waiting or global synchronization barriers.
status: The 2025 foundational work proves that substantial secret-sharing and triple-based families resist super-rushing; no general preservation theorem follows.
why: Addresses a concrete mismatch between round-based proofs and event-driven implementations.
key_works: Asharov–Chandramouli–Cohen–Ishai (2025), [*Peeking Into the Future: MPC Resilient to Super-Rushing Adversaries*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1394).

title: M19. Compositional security against super-rushing
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Give a useful composable security definition and composition theorem for super-rushing protocols, identifying sufficient causal and state-isolation conditions.
status: The 2025 work shows that even sequential composition can fail to preserve super-rushing security.
why: Individually secure subprotocols must remain secure when assembled into larger workflows.
key_works: Asharov–Chandramouli–Cohen–Ishai (2025), [*Peeking Into the Future*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1394); Canetti (2001), [*Universally Composable Security: A New Paradigm for Cryptographic Protocols*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2000/067).

title: M20. Adversarial scheduling corpus for MPC implementations
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Build executable scheduling tests distinguishing rushing, super-rushing, input exclusion, and incorrect abort attribution, with minimized failing traces and proof-model metadata.
status: Proposed data target motivated by documented implementation/proof mismatches and recent asynchronous-correctness distinctions.
why: Would make semantic security regressions reproducible rather than anecdotal.
key_works: Asharov et al. (2025), [*Peeking Into the Future*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1394); Appan–Heath–Ren (2026), [*Asynchronous MPC with Abort*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/455).

title: M21. Complete fairness classification for asymmetric Boolean functionalities
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Characterize exactly which two-party functionalities with potentially different Boolean outputs admit complete fairness, through an effectively checkable criterion and matching constructions or impossibilities.
status: Symmetric Boolean functionalities were classified in 2015. The asymmetric extension and 2017 construction framework leave unresolved cases.
why: Identifies when fairness is possible without an honest majority or trusted intervention.
key_works: Asharov–Beimel–Makriyannis–Omri (2015), [*Complete Characterization of Fairness in Secure Two-Party Computation of Boolean Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/1000); Daza–Makriyannis (2017), [*Designing Fully Secure Protocols for Secure Two-Party Computation of Constant-Domain Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/098).

title: M22. Fairness classification beyond Boolean outputs
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for complete fairness of arbitrary finite-output deterministic and randomized two-party functionalities.
status: Boolean classifications, constant-domain constructions, and reductions to fair coin tossing provide partial structure, without a universal classification.
why: Auctions, exchanges, and private analytics produce richer outputs than a shared bit.
key_works: Daza–Makriyannis (2017), [*Designing Fully Secure Protocols for Secure Two-Party Computation of Constant-Domain Functions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/098); Asharov–Lindell–Rabin (2013), [*Full Characterization of Functions that Imply Fair Coin Tossing and Ramifications to Fairness*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/110).

title: M23. Fairness with a growing dishonest majority
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Characterize efficiently realizable fair symmetric Boolean function families when \(n=\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) and corruption exceeds \(n/2\) by a growing amount.
status: Dachman-Soled obtains broad families at \(n/2\) corruption and majority at \(n/2+c\) for fixed constants \(c\); growing surplus remains distinct.
why: Could identify useful collective decisions remaining fair despite substantial collusion.
key_works: Dachman-Soled (2020), [*Revisiting Fairness in MPC: Polynomial Number of Parties and General Adversarial Structures*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1430).

title: M24. Exact cryptographic strength of a small trusted intervention
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Characterize assumptions necessary and sufficient for general fully secure MPC using a trusted party invoked once whose work is independent of circuit size.
status: The 2022 minimal-trust work gives succinct-FE constructions and lower bounds for restricted approaches; the unrestricted characterization remains open.
why: Determines how much advanced cryptography is needed to minimize trusted computation.
key_works: Ishai–Patra–Patranabis–Ravi–Srinivasan (2022), [*Fully-Secure MPC with Minimal Trust*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1248).

title: M25. Function-specific trusted-party size complexity
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Characterize the minimum once-invoked trusted-party computation needed for each functionality to obtain fairness or guaranteed delivery against dishonest majorities.
status: Proposed classification program extending the 2022 general bounds; useful direct-sum and composition theorems are missing.
why: Could distinguish functions needing substantial trusted intervention from those needing very little.
key_works: Ishai et al. (2022), [*Fully-Secure MPC with Minimal Trust*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1248).

title: M26. Tight delay–security tradeoffs for fair coin tossing
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Determine optimal sequential delay, total work, and adversarial parallelism for delay-enabled fair multiparty coin tossing, including \(n-1\) corruptions.
status: Ball–Christ–Dodis–Garg establish an existence equivalence with delay functions in 2026; tight quantitative reductions remain a separate target.

key_works: Ball–Christ–Dodis–Garg (2026), [*Fair Multiparty Coin Tossing from Minimal Assumptions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/931).

title: M27. Large-party rational coin-tossing classification
subfield: Secure computation: rounds, honesty, and communication
open: Characterize utility matrices admitting cooperative-strategy-proof coin tossing for arbitrary \(n\) against \(n-1\) corruptions, then extend beyond semi-malicious deviations.
status: Wang–Wu’s October 2026 preprint gives sufficient and impossible regimes and a complete three-party characterization; the general-party classification remains open.
why: Determines when economic incentives can support shared randomness despite extensive collusion.
key_works: Wang–Wu (2026), [*Game-Theoretically Fair Coin Toss from Random Walk Against \(n-1\) Corruptions*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2405).

title: M28. Three-round plain-model ZK from polynomial hardness
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct three-message ordinary negligible-error ZK arguments for all NP from conventional polynomial hardness, eliminating the additional keyless multi-collision-resistant-hashing hypothesis.
status: Three-round ZK itself is established. Kiyoshima’s 2026 journal result uses LWE and keyless multi-collision resistance secure against slightly superpolynomial adversaries.
why: Identifies the assumption cost of crossing classical black-box simulation barriers.
key_works: Kiyoshima (2026), [*Public-Coin Three-Round Zero-Knowledge from Learning with Errors and Keyless Multi-Collision-Resistant Hash*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00145-025-09551-8).

title: M29. Complexity-only lower bounds for three-round ZK proofs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Rule out three-round negligible-error ZK proofs for NP using ordinary complexity separations while allowing non-black-box simulation.
status: The 2018 impossibility uses program-obfuscation assumptions. Three-round computationally sound arguments do not settle the proof question.
why: Would distinguish intrinsic interaction limits from consequences of powerful cryptographic assumptions.
key_works: Fleischhacker–Goyal–Jain (2018), [*On the Existence of Three Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/167).

title: M30. Four-round ZK proofs with non-black-box simulation
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Determine whether NP admits four-message negligible-error ZK proofs with code-aware simulation, using a conventional assumption or a matching lower bound.
status: Five-round proofs are known; four-round black-box proofs face lower bounds. Existing three-round impossibilities leave this boundary distinct.
why: Tests whether inspecting verifier code can save a round while retaining unconditional soundness.
key_works: Katz (2008), [*Which Languages Have 4-Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs?*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-78524-8_5); Fleischhacker–Goyal–Jain (2018), [*On the Existence of Three Round Zero-Knowledge Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2018/167).

title: M31. Near-linear honest-verifier-to-malicious-verifier compilation
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Compile efficient honest-verifier ZK into malicious-verifier ZK with near-linear prover and communication overhead and constant additive rounds, stating the privacy notion and extra assumptions.
status: Proposed efficiency target. HV-SZK equals SZK is established, and OWFs already give computational ZK for NP.
why: Would preserve the practical advantage of specialized honest-verifier protocols.
key_works: Goldreich–Sahai–Vadhan (1998), [*Honest-Verifier Statistical Zero-Knowledge Equals General Statistical Zero-Knowledge*](https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~/oded/PSX/gsv.pdf); Vadhan (2006), [*An Unconditional Study of Computational Zero Knowledge*](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539705447207).

title: M32. Constant-round concurrent ZK from ordinary OWFs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Construct constant-round concurrent ZK for NP from arbitrary polynomially secure OWFs in the plain model, with ordinary polynomial-time simulation.
status: OWF-based concurrent protocols and stronger-assumption constant-round protocols exist; the combined target remains open.
why: Would provide low-latency concurrent privacy from the basic symmetric-cryptography assumption.
key_works: Chung–Lin–Pass (2015), [*Constant-Round Concurrent Zero-Knowledge from Indistinguishability Obfuscation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/991); Pass (2021), [*A Tutorial on Concurrent Zero Knowledge*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/615).

title: M33. Exact rounds for fully black-box nonmalleable ZK from OWFs
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Determine the minimum message count for fully black-box simulation-extractable nonmalleable ZK from OWFs, particularly whether five messages suffice with delayed-input one-many security.
status: Constant-round feasibility was established in 2024; four-round fully black-box ordinary ZK from arbitrary OWFs faces an earlier barrier.
why: Separates inherent nonmalleability costs from compiler overhead.
key_works: Botta–Ciampi–Orsini–Siniscalchi–Visconti (2024), [*Black-Box (and Fast) Non-Malleable Zero Knowledge*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/432); Hazay–Pass–Venkitasubramaniam (2020), [*Which Languages Have 4-Round Fully Black-Box Zero-Knowledge Arguments from One-Way Functions?*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-45727-3_20).

title: M34. Four-round statistical nonmalleable ZK from weaker assumptions
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Obtain four-round statistical nonmalleable ZK for NP from arbitrary OWFs, preserving negligible errors and delayed-input one-many simulation extractability.
status: Kiyoshima’s 2025 result, revised in 2026, achieves the target security properties from CRH and injective OWFs.
why: Would combine statistical privacy, low interaction, and minimal assumptions.
key_works: Kiyoshima (2025/2026), [*Four-round Statistical Non-malleable Zero-knowledge*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1787); Kiyoshima (2020), [*Statistical Concurrent Non-Malleable Zero-Knowledge from One-Way Functions*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00145-020-09348-x).

title: M35. Four-round statistical nonmalleable ZK under full concurrency
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Extend four-round statistical nonmalleable ZK to fully concurrent many-many executions, with adaptive statements and a unified simulation-extraction guarantee.
status: The recent four-round theorem establishes delayed-input one-many security; that guarantee does not automatically imply full concurrency.

title: M36. Negligible nonmalleability error in three-round weak ZK
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Obtain three-round plain-model weak-ZK arguments with negligible nonmalleability error, retaining a precisely stated weak-ZK quantifier.
status: A September 2026 preprint obtains three rounds with weak ZK and parameterized inverse-polynomial nonmalleability error from primitives including OT and circuit-private FHE.
why: Would strengthen tamper resistance without adding interaction.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2026), [*Three-Round Weak Non-Malleable Zero-Knowledge Argument*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1964).

title: M37. Constant-round simultaneous resettability from OWFs

title: M38. Low-overhead resettable statistical ZK
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Implement resettable statistical ZK with near-linear prover overhead from a specified witness-encryption instantiation, accounting for witness length, reset count, and security loss.
status: The 2024 equivalence between resettable statistical ZK arguments and witness encryption, assuming OWFs, is qualitative.
why: Would separate unavoidable assumption strength from avoidable implementation cost.
key_works: Kiyoshima (2024), [*Resettable Statistical Zero-Knowledge for NP*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/806).

title: M39. Randomness generation secure under partial resets
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition

status: The October 2026 revision gives generic defenses but identifies partial-reset PRF security as an assumption-level issue.

key_works: Abdolmaleki et al. (2026), [*Resettable Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge: Attacks and Defenses*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1036).

title: M40. End-to-end partial-reset experiments
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition
open: Benchmark selective reuse of prover masks and keys under fault injection and VM rollback, demonstrating a defense with unchanged proof size and verification and under 10% prover overhead across three proof architectures.
status: Proposed experimental target. The 2026 work gives attacks and a generic randomness-generation defense.

key_works: Abdolmaleki et al. (2026), [*Resettable Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge: Attacks and Defenses*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1036).

why: Would show that noninteractive privacy requires no additional primitive beyond generic public-key confidentiality.

title: M42. Fully black-box reusable NIZK from vector trapdoor hashing

title: M50. Ordinary OWFs from high-error private-coin ZK
subfield: Zero knowledge: assumptions, round limits, and robust composition

status: The 2026 result gives ordinary OWFs for public coins but auxiliary-input OWFs for private coins.

why: Would prevent incorrect “solved” labels and invalid composition of incomparable results.

title: A01. Indistinguishability obfuscation from ordinary LWE

title: A02. General iO from one conventional pairing assumption
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Construct general iO from SXDH, DLIN, or another conventional pairing assumption alone, eliminating independent noisy-learning or coding assumptions.

subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Construct general iO using assumptions hard only against polynomial-time adversaries, avoiding subexponential hardness needed to absorb exponential proof losses.
status: Short-equivalence-proof promises permit improved reductions, but arbitrary equivalent circuits do not necessarily satisfy those promises.
why: Would make obfuscation depend on ordinary cryptographic security rather than much stronger quantitative hardness.

title: A04. Minimum truth-table savings sufficient to bootstrap XiO
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Determine whether obfuscations saving only a polynomial factor over truth tables, such as \(2^n/n^c+\operatorname{poly}(|C|,\lambda)\), can bootstrap to polynomial-time iO.
status: XiO with \(2^{(1-\varepsilon)n}\)-type size can be amplified under subexponential XiO and LWE assumptions; polynomial savings are a weaker starting point.

title: A05. General iO from iPRO without extra algebraic assumptions
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Derive general iO from obfuscation for identical pseudorandom functions, iPRO, in the standard model without adding pairing assumptions.

title: A06. Strong pseudorandom obfuscation from falsifiable assumptions
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Construct the stronger PRO variants supporting witness-size-independent witness encryption from clearly specified falsifiable assumptions, or prove a matching barrier.
status: The strongest construction in the PRO framework is heuristic and uses subexponential and private-coin evasive LWE.

key_works: Branco et al. (2024/2025), [*Pseudorandom Obfuscation and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1742).

title: A07. Secret-oblivious private-coin evasive LWE
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Prove security for useful secret-oblivious sampler classes in private-coin evasive LWE, or exhibit an attack satisfying the exact sampler restrictions.
status: The 2026 Huang–Hung–Yamada correction invalidates a previously claimed obfuscation attack in this regime while leaving its security unresolved.
why: Several advanced lattice constructions depend on the precise scope of evasive assumptions.

title: A08. A viable boundary for differing-inputs obfuscation
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Characterize bounded-input circuit samplers admitting diO under conventional falsifiable assumptions when arbitrary correlated auxiliary input is excluded.
status: General auxiliary-input versions face implausibility results. October 2026 public-coin diO uses iO plus the knowledge-style KOALA assumption.
why: Would identify meaningful forms of diO surviving known barriers.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Halevi–Wichs (2014), [*On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/860); Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), [*Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2346).

title: A09. Exact source conditions for compute-and-compare obfuscation
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Characterize the weakest target unpredictability and auxiliary-information conditions supporting compute-and-compare obfuscation from polynomially secure LWE.
status: The 2017 construction covers broad sufficient-pseudoentropy regimes; matching positive and negative boundaries remain incomplete.
why: Applications differ sharply in how predictable their hidden comparison targets are.
key_works: Wichs–Zirdelis (2017), [*Obfuscating Compute-and-Compare Programs under LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2017/276).

title: A10. Quasilinear general iO without equivalence-proof promises
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Achieve quasilinear code size and evaluation overhead for general iO, up to security factors, without assuming short formal proofs that the circuits are equivalent.
status: Ma–Dai–Shi’s 2025 result is quasilinear in both circuit size and equivalence-proof size.
why: Would make asymptotic obfuscation efficiency apply to arbitrary equivalent programs.
key_works: Ma–Dai–Shi (2025), [*Quasi-Linear Indistinguishability Obfuscation via Mathematical Proofs of Equivalence and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/307).

title: A11. A 100-fold-overhead iO demonstrator
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Demonstrate proof-backed general iO with code size and evaluation time each within \(100\times\) baseline at a stated 128-bit classical security target, on a public circuit suite.
status: Proposed moonshot. Feasibility and quasilinear asymptotics do not establish this concrete envelope.
why: Would turn general obfuscation from a theoretical capability into an experimentally assessable technology.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2020/2021), [*Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09317); Ma–Dai–Shi (2025), [*Quasi-Linear Indistinguishability Obfuscation*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/307).

title: A12. Obfuscation-assumption challenge corpus
subfield: Obfuscation: assumptions, restricted notions, and efficiency
open: Publish machine-readable challenge families with exact sampler restrictions, parameter provenance, known attacks, reduced instances, and reproducible attack costs.
status: Proposed data target. Recent corrections to evasive-LWE attack claims demonstrate why sampler metadata is essential.
why: Would make assumption comparisons and cryptanalysis more reliable.
key_works: Huang–Hung–Yamada (2026), [*A Note on Obfuscation-Based Attacks on Private-Coin Evasive LWE*](https://cic.iacr.org/p/2/4/20); Ragavan–Vafa–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [*Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Bilinear Maps and LPN Variants*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/856).

title: A13. Fully collusion-resistant circuit FE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Construct public-key FE for arbitrary circuits from LWE, secure against any polynomial number of key queries, with ciphertext size independent of both collusion count and supported circuit size.
status: General compact FE follows from stronger obfuscation-related assumptions; bounded-collusion minimal-assumption FE has collusion-dependent ciphertexts.
why: Would enable general controlled disclosure under a conventional lattice assumption.
key_works: Garg et al. (2013/2016), [*Candidate Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption for all Circuits*](https://doi.org/10.1137/14095772X); Ananth–Vaikuntanathan (2019), [*Optimal Bounded-Collusion Secure Functional Encryption*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/314).

title: A14. Crossing the linear-collusion ciphertext barrier
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Achieve genuinely sublinear ciphertext dependence on the collusion bound \(Q\) for general-circuit FE from weak assumptions, or sharpen barriers for restricted functionality classes.
status: Adaptive bounded-collusion FE achieves linear dependence on \(Q\); improving it in the general setting would imply iO.
why: Determines when compactness itself demands obfuscation-level power.
key_works: Ananth–Vaikuntanathan (2019), [*Optimal Bounded-Collusion Secure Functional Encryption*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/314).

title: A15. Fully adaptive circuit ABE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Construct circuit ABE from ordinary LWE with full adaptive security for challenge attributes and function-key requests after public parameters are known.
status: October 2026 output-adaptive ABE is an intermediate notion. Fully adaptive constructions using witness encryption do not settle LWE alone.

key_works: Waters–Wichs (2024), [*Adaptively Secure Attribute-Based Encryption from Witness Encryption*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1486); Cheng–Goyal (2026), [*Revisiting Partitioning: Output-Adaptive ABE for Circuits from LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2305).

title: A16. Unleveled ABE from ordinary circular LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Obtain fully collusion-resistant ABE for unbounded-depth circuits from ordinary LWE plus conventional circular security, without evasive-circular assumptions.
status: Ordinary circular security gives unbounded-depth single-key FE, single-key ABE, and reusable garbling; full ABE and predicate encryption use evasive-circular LWE.
why: Would remove a predetermined depth ceiling without escalating to a specialized assumption.
key_works: Hsieh–Lin–Luo (2023/2025), [*Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices: Garbled Circuits of Optimal Size, Laconic Functional Evaluation, and More*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1716).

title: A17. Simultaneously optimal circuit-ABE components
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Make the cryptographic portions of public parameters, ciphertexts, and secret keys simultaneously independent of policy size and depth under ordinary LWE, allowing public descriptions externally.
status: Polynomial-in-security-parameter keys are known; small keys alone do not give the full simultaneous compactness target.
why: Optimizing one component can merely move the cost into another.
key_works: Cini–Wee (2023/2025), [*ABE for Circuits with poly(\(\lambda\))-Sized Keys from LWE*](https://doi.org/10.1137/24M1636162); Hsieh–Lin–Luo (2023/2025), [*Attribute-Based Encryption for Circuits of Unbounded Depth from Lattices*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1716).

title: A18. Fully attribute-hiding predicate encryption for circuits
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness

key_works: Gorbunov–Vaikuntanathan–Wee (2015), [*Predicate Encryption for Circuits from LWE*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-48000-7_25).

title: A19. General registered FE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Construct fully collusion-resistant registered FE for circuits from LWE, with independently generated user keys and succinct aggregation by an untrusted curator.
status: General constructions use powerful primitives; recent lattice results cover pseudorandom functionalities or bounded-collusion settings under additional assumptions.
why: Would remove central secret-key generation from general functional encryption.
key_works: Pal–Schädlich–Tairi (2025), [*Registered Functional Encryption for Pseudorandom Functionalities from Lattices*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/967); Zhang–Chen–He–Zhang (2024/2025), [*Bounded Collusion-Resistant Registered Functional Encryption for Circuits*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/1572).

title: A20. Sublinear collusion dependence in lattice registered FE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Reduce ciphertext dependence on corrupted-user count \(Q\) below linear while retaining general circuits and explicit lattice assumptions.
status: The 2026 construction achieves \(Q\widetilde O(d)+\ell\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,d,\log N)\) ciphertext size from decomposed LWE in the random-oracle model.
why: Large collusion bounds otherwise dominate the compactness budget.
key_works: Champion–Wu–Yamada (2026), [*Silent Threshold Encryption from Lattices*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1716).

title: A21. Depth-independent registered ABE from succinct LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Remove circuit-depth factors from registered circuit ABE based on succinct LWE, retaining succinct parameters and unbounded polynomially many users.
status: Wee–Wu achieve \(\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,d,\log N)\)-size components; depth-independent alternatives use stronger machinery.
why: Would avoid choosing resource budgets around the deepest future policy.
key_works: Wee–Wu (2025), [*Unbounded Distributed Broadcast Encryption and Registered ABE from Succinct LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1039).

title: A22. Adaptive registered ABE with linear CRS in the plain model
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Obtain pairing-based registered ABE for monotone span programs with linear CRS, adaptive security, and independent stateless user key generation in the plain model.
status: The 2026 linear-CRS construction has static plain-model security under a \(q\)-type assumption and adaptive security in random oracles.
why: Would combine compact setup with realistic adaptive use.
key_works: Stracovsky–Waters–Wu (2026), [*Pairing-Based Registered ABE for Boolean Formulas with a Linear-Size CRS*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1062).

title: A23. Remove random oracles from succinct registered circuit ABE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Achieve the nearly optimal registered-circuit-ABE parameter envelope from succinct LWE in the plain model, supporting unbounded polynomially many independent user keys.
status: The relevant 2025 constructions use random oracles; removing depth dependence is a separate problem.
why: Would replace idealized hashing with a concrete standard-model foundation.
key_works: Wee–Wu (2025), [*Unbounded Distributed Broadcast Encryption and Registered ABE from Succinct LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1039); Champion–Hsieh–Wu (2025), [*Registered ABE and Adaptively-Secure Broadcast Encryption from Succinct LWE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/044).

title: A24. Fully adaptive multi-authority circuit ABE from LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Construct decentralized circuit ABE from ordinary LWE with adaptive security against malicious authorities, without random oracles or a central authority.
status: Formula-level results are stronger on several security axes; 2025 circuit constructions use very-selective security, stronger assumptions, and restricted authority corruption.

title: A25. Malicious-client-secure circuit multi-client ABE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Obtain adaptive multi-client circuit ABE tolerating substantial malicious-client participation, with independent encryption and secure binding of ciphertext combinations to identifiers.
status: The 2025 introduction provides circuit constructions with limited adaptivity and corrupted-client security.

key_works: Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), [*Lattice-based Multi-Authority/Client Attribute-based Encryption for Circuits*](https://cic.iacr.org/p/1/4/1).

title: A26. Compact multi-authority FE across the corruption frontier
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness

title: A27. General multi-input FE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness
open: Construct compact multi-input FE for arbitrary circuits from LWE, supporting repeated ciphertexts and security for all authorized cross-combinations.

title: A28. Function privacy without universal-circuit inflation
subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness

subfield: Functional encryption, attribute-based encryption, and compactness

status: Proposed data target. Existing constructions occupy different points on these axes, making raw throughput comparisons misleading.
why: Would make implementation progress comparable across genuinely equivalent security tasks.

title: A30. Witness encryption for NP from ordinary LWE
open: Construct polynomial-time WE for all NP from ordinary LWE, without evasive-LWE hypotheses.
status: Open since WE’s 2013 introduction. Direct lattice candidates use evasive assumptions; recent generic-group results address a different model.

title: A36. Breaking the half-exponent in LWE-based XWE

status: The \(2^{m/2}\) construction is a verified reference point; arbitrarily small positive exponents are a stronger target.

open: From plain WE and conventional auxiliaries, encrypt to arbitrary monotone circuits over \(K\) NP instances with cryptographic payload polynomial in \(\lambda\), one-instance complexity, and \(\log K\).
status: CNF/DNF policies follow from weaker tools; broader bounded-space policies use iO. Public policy descriptions remain external.

key_works: Garg et al. (2025), [*A Framework for Witness Encryption from Linearly Verifiable SNARKs and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1364); Campanelli (2026), [*A Note on Extractable Witness Encryption in Generic Groups*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2399).

title: A42. Efficient public certification of condition ciphertexts
open: Provide compact public certificates that special-purpose WE ciphertexts encode the declared payload commitment and condition, with at most \(10\times\) encryption overhead and malicious-encryptor security.
status: Proposed engineering target. General proofs can certify encryption computations, but the integrated efficient envelope remains to be demonstrated.
why: Users must be able to trust what a conditional ciphertext promises to release.
key_works: Garg et al. (2025), [*A Framework for Witness Encryption from Linearly Verifiable SNARKs and Applications*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/1364).

title: A43. SNARGs for all NP from polynomially hard LWE
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Construct SNARGs for arbitrary NP from ordinary polynomial-hardness LWE, with polynomial preprocessing and proof length polynomial in security and logarithmic in verification time.
status: LWE-based SNARGs for P and special NP languages with suitable bounded-space nonmembership proofs are established.
why: Would provide general succinct verification from a conventional post-quantum assumption.
key_works: Jin–Kalai–Lombardi–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [*SNARGs under LWE via Propositional Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/956).

title: A44. Adaptive NP SNARGs from polynomial-security iO
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Derive adaptively sound NP SNARGs from polynomially secure iO and OWFs, eliminating subexponential hardness from the implication.
status: Waters–Wu’s 2025 theorem establishes the implication using subexponentially secure iO and OWFs without an extra algebraic assumption.
why: Would reduce the hardness needed for broadly adaptive succinct verification.
key_works: Waters–Wu (2024/2025), [*A Pure Indistinguishability Obfuscation Approach to Adaptively-Sound SNARGs for NP*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/933).

title: A45. Universal SNARGs without formal-correctness promises
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Obtain universal NP SNARGs from arbitrary suitable WE or two-message arguments without requiring short correctness proofs in a specified formal system.
status: The 2025 universal framework uses formal proofs of correctness; non-explicit use of a scheme does not eliminate that logical requirement.
why: Would make universal cryptographic constructions less dependent on formal provability.
key_works: Jin–Kalai–Lombardi–Mathialagan (2025), [*Universal SNARGs for NP from Proofs of Correctness*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3717823.3718104).

title: A46. Remove derandomization from unprovability-based SNARGs
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Eliminate \(\mathrm{prBPP}=\mathrm{prP}\) from the 2026 unprovability-based NP-SNARG construction while retaining its other explicitly stated premises.
status: The construction uses LWE, SXDH, promise-class derandomization, and a formal unprovability assumption involving hard Extended Frege tautologies.
why: Isolates whether derandomization contributes essential cryptographic power.
key_works: Hsieh–Jain–Li–Mathialagan (2026), [*SNARGs for NP from Unprovability of Mathematical Theorems*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/098/).

title: A47. Adaptive public delegation from plain WE
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Construct publicly verifiable, adaptively sound SNARGs for arbitrary NP from plain WE plus ordinary LWE, without replacing WE by extractable WE or iO.
status: Universal constructions give nonadaptive results and stronger guarantees for restricted languages. Positional WE alone does not establish the full target.
why: Would turn a weaker advanced primitive into broadly usable adaptive delegation.
key_works: Jin et al. (2025), [*Universal SNARGs for NP from Proofs of Correctness*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3717823.3718104); Nassar–Waters–Wu (2026), [*Obfuscating Non-Evasive Programs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1932).

title: A48. Function-statistically-binding commitments from LWE
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Construct succinct function vector commitments with the function statistical binding needed by shadow PCPs from ordinary LWE or comparably conventional assumptions.
status: Guan–Yogev’s 2026 revision instantiates Micali’s SNARG assuming LWE plus these commitments and identifies weaker-assumption commitments as a remaining target.
why: Could remove a specialized assumption from a central route to succinct arguments.
key_works: Guan–Yogev (2025/2026), [*Micali’s SNARG, Function Vector Commitments, and Fiat–Shamir*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2328).

title: A49. Adaptive soundness for shadow-PCP SNARGs
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Upgrade the shadow-PCP/function-binding route to adaptively sound Micali-style SNARGs while retaining standard-model hashing and succinct parameters.
status: The September 2026 theorem establishes nonadaptive soundness.
why: Verifiers should remain secure when statements are selected after setup is published.
key_works: Guan–Yogev (2025/2026), [*Micali’s SNARG, Function Vector Commitments, and Fiat–Shamir*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2328).

title: A50. Amplifying mild succinctness without knowledge extraction
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Generically amplify mildly succinct, ordinarily sound noninteractive arguments into fully succinct SNARGs without assuming knowledge soundness.
status: The 2025 “Boosting SNARKs” theorem uses a SNARK as its starting object; ordinary soundness is a separate target.
why: Would show that compact verification can amplify without a witness-extraction premise.
key_works: Cheng–Goyal (2025), [*Boosting SNARKs and Rate-1 Barrier in Arguments of Knowledge*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2025.56).

title: A51. Practical two-group-element SNARGs
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Retain two-source-group-element proofs while achieving quasilinear prover work, tractable CRS generation, and competitive verification on large circuits.
status: The 2025/2026 construction gives two \(\mathbb G_1\) elements in GGM+ROM, including a 768-bit BLS12-381 illustration, but is explicitly not yet concretely efficient.
why: Would make ultra-short proofs useful beyond an asymptotic feasibility demonstration.
key_works: Arnon–Dujmovic–Yogev (2025/2026), [*Pairing-Based SNARGs with Two Group Elements*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2160).

title: A52. The unrestricted one-group-element SNARG boundary
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Extend one-element proof lower bounds to broader verifier classes, or construct a SNARG outside the currently excluded classes.
status: Existing lower bounds apply in Maurer GGM+ROM under natural verifier restrictions and OWFs; they are not fully unrestricted impossibility theorems.
why: Would identify the true minimum size of algebraic succinct proofs.
key_works: Arnon–Dujmovic–Yogev (2025/2026), [*Pairing-Based SNARGs with Two Group Elements*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2160); Barta–Ishai–Ostrovsky–Wu (2020), [*On Succinct Arguments and Witness Encryption from Groups*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1319).

title: A53. Quasioptimal concrete delegation from polynomial LWE
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Implement LWE-based SNARGs or IVC for deterministic computations with quasilinear prover work, proofs below 1 MB, and verification below 1% of recomputation on declared large workloads.
status: Proposed moonshot retaining polynomial-hardness assumptions. Theoretical LWE-based SNARGs and IVC for P already exist.
why: Would provide a concrete alternative to pairing- or hash-based delegation.
key_works: Chen–Freitag–Jin–Wichs (2025), [*Unambiguous SNARGs for P from LWE with Applications to PPAD Hardness*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3717823.3718159).

title: A54. A fully doubly efficient IP equals PSPACE theorem
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: For polynomial-space computations of general time \(T\), construct information-theoretic interactive proofs with prover time polynomial in \(T\) and verifier time polynomial in original input length.
status: Chen–Hong–Kalai–Xi reach \(T(n)=n^{O(\log n)}\) in 2026, improving the earlier \(n^{O(\sqrt{\log n/\log\log n})}\) regime.
why: Would align honest proving cost with actual computation throughout PSPACE.
key_works: Chen–Hong–Kalai–Xi (2026), [*Towards a Doubly Efficient IP=PSPACE*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1287).

title: A55. Covert memory checking without read-only reads
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Establish matching overhead lower bounds when logical reads may modify server memory or private checker state, or exploit that freedom to beat current bounds.
status: The 2025 \(\Omega(\log n/\log\log n)\) query lower bound assumes read-only reads and sublinear local storage.
why: Determines whether mutable reads enable fundamentally cheaper integrity checking.
key_works: Boyle–Komargodski–Vafa (2025), [*The Complexity of Memory Checking with Covert Security*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/358).

title: A56. Proof-checked implementation of assumption-based delegation
subfield: Succinct arguments, delegation, and computation checking
open: Connect a standard-assumption SNARG implementation to a machine-checked specification covering arithmetization, preprocessing, transcript binding, adaptive statements, and serialization.
status: Proposed engineering target. Verifying an arithmetic kernel alone does not establish end-to-end protocol security.
why: Would close the gap between asymptotic proofs and deployed verifiers.
key_works: Jin–Kalai–Lombardi–Vaikuntanathan (2024), [*SNARGs under LWE via Propositional Proofs*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/956); Guan–Yogev (2025/2026), [*Micali’s SNARG, Function Vector Commitments, and Fiat–Shamir*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2328).

title: E01. Sharp entropy threshold for explicit two-source extraction
open: Match the probabilistic existence threshold—including leading constants and error dependence—for polynomial-time extraction from two independent n-bit sources.
status: Li achieved asymptotically optimal \(O(\log n)\) entropy in 2023; sharp constants and joint error/output guarantees remain stronger targets.
why: Determines exactly how little independent randomness suffices for explicit extraction.
key_works: Li (2023), [*Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06802).

title: E02. Negligible-error two-source extraction at polylogarithmic entropy
open: Construct explicit two-source extractors with \(k=\operatorname{polylog}(n)\) entropy and error \(n^{-\omega(1)}\), ideally \(2^{-k^c}\) for constant \(c>0\).
status: Low-entropy constant-error advances do not give this guarantee; known low-error constructions require substantially more entropy.
why: Cryptographic applications often need negligible rather than constant or inverse-polynomial error.
key_works: Chattopadhyay–Zuckerman (2016/2019), [*Explicit Two-Source Extractors and Resilient Functions*](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2019/189-3/p01); Doron–Fridman (2025), [*Bit-Fixing Extractors for Almost-Logarithmic Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.33).

title: E03. Almost-all entropy output at logarithmic entropy
open: At \(k=O(\log n)\), extract \(k-O(\log(1/\varepsilon))\) bits while remaining strong in a designated source, with near-optimal constants.
status: One-bit logarithmic-entropy extraction does not establish this simultaneous output, strength, and error guarantee.
why: Would turn very weak sources into useful multi-bit random seeds.
key_works: Li (2023), [*Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06802); Cohen–Doron–Samocha (2025), [*Seed-Protecting Extractors*](https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v021a008/).

title: E04. Bit-fixing extraction at the sharp low-entropy boundary
open: Remove remaining polylogarithmic overhead in the entropy requirement for explicit oblivious bit-fixing extractors, retaining long output and low error in feasible parameter regimes.
status: Doron–Fridman achieve almost-logarithmic entropy with long output and low error in 2025.
why: Bit-fixing sources model randomness with unknown deterministic coordinates.
key_works: Doron–Fridman (2025), [*Bit-Fixing Extractors for Almost-Logarithmic Entropy*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.33).

title: E05. Explicit low-degree sumset extractors near random-polynomial bounds
open: Deterministically construct low-degree polynomials matching the entropy/error regimes achieved by random polynomials on sumset sources.
status: The 2025 random-polynomial framework gives strong existence theorems; deterministic explicitness remains distinct.
why: Would translate algebraic existence into usable low-complexity extractors.
key_works: Alrabiah–Goodman–Mosheiff–Ribeiro (2025), [*Low-Degree Polynomials Are Good Extractors*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.38).

title: E06. Explicit low-degree extractors for polynomial sources
open: Construct low-degree extractors for bounded-degree polynomial-map sources near random-construction bounds, uniformly over the specified source-degree class.
status: Random low-degree polynomials achieve important regimes; removing construction randomness remains open.
why: Algebraically generated randomness appears throughout coding and cryptography.
key_works: Alrabiah–Goodman–Mosheiff–Ribeiro (2025), [*Low-Degree Polynomials Are Good Extractors*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.38).

title: E07. Explicit extraction from bounded-complexity varieties
open: Construct deterministic extractors for uniform distributions on common zero sets of bounded-degree polynomials, with useful dimension and degree dependence.
status: Random-polynomial existence results cover new variety-source regimes; uniform explicit constructions remain a target.
why: Would exploit geometric structure in sources beyond affine spaces.
key_works: Alrabiah–Goodman–Mosheiff–Ribeiro (2025), [*Low-Degree Polynomials Are Good Extractors*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2025.38).

title: E08. Two good sources among many adversarial sources
open: Extract with negligible error when only two unknown members of a long independent-source sequence have polylogarithmic entropy and the rest may be fixed adversarially.
status: Chattopadhyay–Goodman obtain three good low-entropy sources in 2025; their two-good-source consequence requires higher entropy.
why: Would support robust randomness generation without knowing which contributors are useful.
key_works: Chattopadhyay–Goodman (2025), [*Leakage-Resilient Extractors against Number-on-Forehead Protocols*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2025/075/).

title: E09. Samplable-source extraction from weaker circuit hardness
open: Replace nondeterministic exponential circuit-hardness assumptions in multiplicative-error extraction for samplable sources by deterministic circuit hardness.
status: Shaltiel’s 2025 analysis explains why current techniques generate pseudorandomness against nondeterministic circuits and therefore use stronger premises.
why: Would weaken the complexity assumptions needed to clean algorithmically generated randomness.
key_works: Shaltiel (2025), [*Multiplicative Extractors for Samplable Distributions*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.22).

title: E10. Near-optimal low-entropy samplable-source extraction
open: Under a clearly stated standard circuit-hardness hypothesis, extract many bits with small error from polynomial-circuit-samplable sources having near-logarithmic entropy.
status: Low-entropy one-bit results and higher-entropy multiplicative-error results leave the joint target open. The separate 2026 near-optimality report was retracted.
why: Would provide strong extraction from sources described by efficient algorithms rather than simple algebraic structure.
key_works: Oh–Shaltiel (2025/2026), [*Extractors for Samplable Distributions from the Two-Source Extractor Recipe*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2025/107/); Shaltiel (2025), [*Multiplicative Extractors for Samplable Distributions*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.22); [ECCC TR26-089 retraction](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/089/).

title: E11. Simultaneously optimal seeded-extractor parameters
subfield: Seeded extraction: sharp parameters and computational complexity
open: Match optimal seed length and entropy loss to additive \(O(1)\) simultaneously throughout the feasible \((n,k,\varepsilon)\) range with uniform polynomial-time strong extractors.
status: Constant-factor-optimal constructions are classical; sharp simultaneous optimality is stronger.
why: Would settle the basic efficiency frontier for converting weak randomness into uniform bits.
key_works: Guruswami–Umans–Vadhan (2009), [*Unbalanced Expanders and Randomness Extractors from Parvaresh–Vardy Codes*](https://doi.org/10.1145/1538902.1538904); Vadhan (2012), [*Pseudorandomness*](https://people.seas.harvard.edu/~salil/pseudorandomness/).

title: E12. Short seeds, low error, and sublinear entropy loss
subfield: Seeded extraction: sharp parameters and computational complexity
open: Achieve seed length \(O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\) and entropy loss \(o(k)\) for negligible error when \(\log(1/\varepsilon)=o(k)\), preferably with nearly linear evaluation.
status: Doron–Ribeiro achieve \((1-\eta)k\) output for fixed \(\eta>0\) in their regime; sublinear loss is explicitly open.
why: Would preserve nearly all available entropy at cryptographic error levels.
key_works: Doron–Ribeiro (2025/2026), [*Nearly-Linear Time Seeded Extractors with Short Seeds*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07473).

title: E13. Preprocessing-free nearly linear extraction
subfield: Seeded extraction: sharp parameters and computational complexity
open: Remove parameter-dependent preprocessing from short-seed nearly linear extractors in very-low-entropy and very-small-error regimes.
status: The February 2026 revision identifies this as future work; other parameter regimes already avoid preprocessing.
why: Preprocessing can dominate small deployments or frequently changing parameters.
key_works: Doron–Ribeiro (2025/2026), [*Nearly-Linear Time Seeded Extractors with Short Seeds*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07473).

title: E14. The low-entropy AC⁰ extractor frontier
subfield: Seeded extraction: sharp parameters and computational complexity
open: Characterize optimal entropy, seed, error, and depth tradeoffs for uniform AC⁰ strong extractors below \(n/\operatorname{polylog}n\) entropy.
status: Cheng–Wu obtain strong parameters in their high-entropy AC⁰ regime and NC¹ constructions; lower-entropy constant-depth tradeoffs remain incomplete.
why: Would determine how much extraction can be performed by extremely shallow circuits.
key_works: Cheng–Wu (2024), [*Randomness Extractors in AC⁰ and NC¹*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.APPROX/RANDOM.2024.69).

title: E15. Restricted nonmalleability to full nonmalleability
subfield: Seeded extraction: sharp parameters and computational complexity
open: Determine whether security against permutation—or merely involution—seed tampering implies full nonmalleability against arbitrary fixed-point-free tampering with controlled losses.
status: Explicitly posed by Cohen–Doron–Samocha in 2025.
why: Could simplify the construction and analysis of nonmalleable extractors.
key_works: Cohen–Doron–Samocha (2025), [*Seed-Protecting Extractors*](https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v021a008/).

title: E16. Small exceptional-seed sets from restricted nonmalleability
subfield: Seeded extraction: sharp parameters and computational complexity
open: Show that restricted nonmalleability permits removal of a small seed set so every remaining distinct seed pair produces jointly near-uniform outputs, or refute this implication.
status: Explicit 2025 question; average-over-seed security does not directly imply uniform pairwise guarantees.
why: Would support reliable seed reuse and stronger structural extractor properties.
key_works: Cohen–Doron–Samocha (2025), [*Seed-Protecting Extractors*](https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v021a008/).

title: P01. Polylogarithmic two-server information-theoretic PIR
open: Construct two-server PIR for arbitrary N-bit databases with polylogarithmic total communication and information-theoretic single-server privacy, without free correlated setup.
status: Dvir–Gopi achieve \(\exp(O(\sqrt{\log N\log\log N}))\) communication; the gap to logarithmic lower bounds remains enormous.
why: Would enable very short private queries without computational assumptions.
key_works: Dvir–Gopi (2014/2016), [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692).

title: P02. Superlogarithmic unrestricted two-server PIR lower bounds
open: Prove superlogarithmic total-communication lower bounds allowing long answers, nonlinear protocols, and unrestricted server computation.
status: Stronger lower bounds require additional answer-size, algebraic, or probe restrictions.
why: Would reveal whether current subpolynomial upper bounds are remotely optimal.
key_works: Dvir–Gopi (2016), [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692); Kolby–Roy–Sternad–Yakoubov (2025), [*Information-Theoretic Random-Index PIR*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITC.2025.5).

title: P03. Sparse decoding polynomials for all server counts
open: Remove the number-theoretic conjecture from the improved \(s\)-server PIR tradeoff for every fixed \(s\), and make constructions uniform as \(s\) grows.
status: Gupte–Ragavan’s July 2026 result conditionally achieves \(\exp(O((\log N)^{1/s}(\log\log N)^{1-1/s}))\) communication, unconditionally for fixed \(s\le15\).
why: Could substantially reduce server requirements for highly efficient PIR.
key_works: Gupte–Ragavan (2026), [*Exponentially Fewer-Server PIR from Sparser S-Decoding Polynomials*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22033).

title: P04. Sublinear-time, short-message PIR with near-linear storage
open: Simultaneously achieve two-server information-theoretic privacy, \(N\operatorname{polylog}N\) storage, \(N^{1-\delta}\) online probes for fixed \(\delta>0\), and polylogarithmic communication.
status: Henzinger–Ragavan achieve quasilinear storage and sublinear probes; their stronger communication reduction invokes computational encryption.
why: Efficient communication alone does not prevent servers from scanning the database.
key_works: Henzinger–Ragavan (2026), [*Two-Server Private Information Retrieval in Sublinear Time and Quasilinear Space*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2008).

title: P05. Dynamic information-theoretic PIR with cheap updates
open: Maintain quasilinear-space, sublinear-query-time information-theoretic PIR under point updates with polylogarithmic amortized update cost and explicit update leakage.
status: Proposed dynamic extension of recent static preprocessing advances.
why: Real private databases change; expensive rebuilding can erase query-time gains.
key_works: Henzinger–Ragavan (2026), [*Two-Server Private Information Retrieval in Sublinear Time and Quasilinear Space*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/2008); Beimel–Ishai–Malkin (2000), *Reducing the Servers’ Computation in Private Information Retrieval: PIR with Preprocessing*.

title: P06. Arithmetic two-server PIR below the cube-root bound
open: Beat \(O(N^{1/3})\) transmitted field elements for a database of N field elements using only black-box field arithmetic, or prove this optimal.
status: The 2026 arithmetic-PIR characterization explicitly leaves this two-server boundary open; nontrivial single-server arithmetic PIR is already ruled out.
why: Determines the limitations of a broad algebraic design approach.
key_works: Applebaum–Ishai–Shechter (2026), [*On Arithmetic Private Information Retrieval: Why Code-Based PIR (Usually) Fails*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1224).

title: P07. Tight noninteractive random-index PIR communication
open: Close the gap between the \(\Omega(\sqrt d\,w)\) lower bound and upper bounds for two-server, one-message-per-server random-index PIR on d rows of w bits.
status: Kolby et al. establish this lower bound and sublinear constructions in appropriate row-width regimes in 2025.
why: Random-index retrieval supports private sampling with a different interaction pattern from chosen-index PIR.
key_works: Kolby–Roy–Sternad–Yakoubov (2025), [*Information-Theoretic Random-Index PIR*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITC.2025.5).

title: P08. General finite-file MDS-TPIR capacity
open: Determine exact download capacity for separately MDS-coded files with T colluding servers across all feasible parameters, without restricting to linear full-support-rank schemes.
status: The original general formula was disproved. New 2026 cases and restricted linear-capacity results leave the general problem open.
why: Would quantify the optimal download cost of privacy in coded storage.
key_works: Freij-Hollanti et al. (2017), [*Private Information Retrieval from Coded Databases with Colluding Servers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.02062); Sun–Tao–Xu–Zhang (2026), [*A Disguise-and-Squeeze PIR Scheme for the MDS-TPIR Setting and Beyond*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.10769).

title: P09. Capacity of joint MDS-coded PIR
open: Characterize optimal private retrieval when files are jointly encoded across storage nodes, beyond known systematic-storage patterns and parameter cases.
status: Joint coding can outperform separate-file schemes; 2026 results determine selected regimes and improve others.
why: Joint encoding may change the fundamental storage/privacy/download tradeoff.
key_works: Xu–Shi–Lan–Fang (2026), [*Private Information Retrieval from Joint Systematic MDS-Coded with Non-Colluding Servers: Bounds and Constructions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22802).

title: P10. Superpolynomial lower bounds for constant-query LDCs
open: Prove superpolynomial block length for binary locally decodable codes correcting a constant error fraction with every fixed query count, or construct a counterexample.
status: General lower bounds remain far below known superpolynomial constructions; restricted linear or low-query results do not settle all cases.
why: This coding question directly constrains information-theoretic private retrieval.
key_works: Goldreich (2024), *Lower Bounds on the Length of Locally Decodable Codes*, in [*Open Problems in Honor of Luca Trevisan*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3710795.3710799); Dvir–Gopi (2016), [*2-Server PIR with Sub-Polynomial Communication*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6692).

title: C01. Logarithmic-overhead universal randomized compression
open: Reduce universal polynomial-time randomized-compression overhead to \(O(\log(n/\varepsilon))\), given a target description length and error \(\varepsilon\).
status: Polynomial-time constructions achieve \(O(\log m\cdot\log(n/\varepsilon))\) overhead; logarithmic overhead is known with prohibitively slow compression.
why: Would approach information-theoretic optimality without sacrificing efficient encoding.
key_works: Bauwens (2018), [*Optimal Probabilistic Polynomial Time Compression and the Slepian-Wolf Theorem: Tighter Version and Simple Proofs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.00750); Bauwens–Zimand (2019/2023), [*Universal Almost Optimal Compression and Slepian-Wolf Coding in Probabilistic Polynomial Time*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.04268).

title: C02. Efficient decoding under time-bounded compression promises
open: Characterize source and decoder classes admitting both near-optimal randomized compression and polynomial-time decompression relative to a time-bounded description measure.
status: Universal compression can slow decoding; unrestricted uncomputable Kolmogorov complexity cannot supply the required efficient promise.
why: A short encoding is operationally useful only when the intended receiver can decode it.
key_works: Bauwens–Zimand (2019/2023), [*Universal Almost Optimal Compression and Slepian-Wolf Coding in Probabilistic Polynomial Time*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.04268); Zimand (2024), [*On One-Way Functions and the Average Time Complexity of Almost-Optimal Compression*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.03392).

title: C03. Compression and extraction with reused public seeds
open: Determine tight entropy-loss and seed-refresh requirements when later weak sources depend on earlier outputs generated using the same public seed, under explicit bounded-dependence models.
status: Extractor-dependent-source and seed-protection frameworks handle particular dependence classes; arbitrary seed dependence cannot be allowed.
why: Real systems reuse parameters and continuously process correlated data.
key_works: Dodis–Vaikuntanathan–Wichs (2019/2020), [*Extracting Randomness from Extractor-Dependent Sources*](https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/1339); Cohen–Doron–Samocha (2025), [*Seed-Protecting Extractors*](https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v021a008/).

title: I01. Practical short-seed extraction at cryptographic error
subfield: Infrastructure for pseudorandomness and assumption research
open: Demonstrate at least a tenfold time or memory improvement over a pinned short-seed-extractor baseline at identical \((n,k,m,\varepsilon)\), with \(\varepsilon\le2^{-128}\).
status: Proposed moonshot. Nearly linear short-seed theory and existing extractor libraries provide starting points.
why: Would make strong theoretical extractors usable in high-throughput cryptographic systems.
key_works: Doron–Ribeiro (2025/2026), [*Nearly-Linear Time Seeded Extractors with Short Seeds*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07473); Foreman–Yeung–Edgington–Curchod (2025), [*Cryptomite: A Versatile and User-Friendly Library of Randomness Extractors*](https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2025-01-08-1584).

title: I02. Machine-checkable cryptographic implication census
subfield: Infrastructure for pseudorandomness and assumption research
open: Build at least 1,000 versioned implication and separation records encoding quantifiers, setup, uniformity, adversary class, reduction type, and security loss, with consistency checks.
status: Proposed data target. A bibliography does not establish that theorem statements can safely be composed.
why: Supplies reusable infrastructure for a much larger cross-linked open-problem census.
key_works: Couteau–Farshim–Mahmoody (2021), [*Black-Box Uselessness: Composing Separations in Cryptography*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2021.47); Bitansky–Degwekar (2019), [*On the Complexity of Collision Resistant Hash Functions: New and Old Black-Box Separations*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-36030-6_17).

title: I03. Reproducible implementations of OWF-to-PRG reductions
subfield: Infrastructure for pseudorandomness and assumption research
open: Implement at least three foundational transformations with symbolic security-loss accounting, runtime/randomness measurements, and controlled preimage-distribution test cases.
status: Proposed engineering benchmark. Asymptotic constructions leave concrete constants and crossover points largely unspecified.
why: Would expose which generic reductions are usable and where their actual costs arise.
key_works: Håstad–Impagliazzo–Levin–Luby (1999), [*A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function*](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539793244708); Mazor–Zhang (2024), [*Simple Constructions from (Almost) Regular One-Way Functions*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00145-024-09507-4).

title: G01. Ta-Shma’s polynomial quantum-error blowup conjecture
open: Prove that every classical strong extractor with m output bits and error \(\varepsilon\) is quantum-proof with error \(O(m\sqrt\varepsilon)\), allowing the stipulated logarithmic extra entropy, or give a counterexample.
status: Studied since the 2000s; general lifting bounds have exponential output-length dependence.
why: Would let broad classes of classical extractors be safely reused against quantum side information.
key_works: Berta–Fawzi–Scholz (2017), [*Quantum-proof randomness extractors via operator space theory*](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2016.2627531), [arXiv:1409.3563](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.3563).

title: G02. Bound the dimension of the worst quantum extractor adversary
open: For a finite extractor table and accuracy \(\eta\), bound the quantum side-information dimension needed to approximate maximum distinguishing advantage within \(\eta\), ideally polynomially.
status: Explicitly posed in 2017; norm formulations and semidefinite relaxations do not generally control this dimension.
why: Would make finite-instance quantum-security certification computationally tractable.
key_works: Berta–Fawzi–Scholz (2017), [*Quantum-proof randomness extractors via operator space theory*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.3563).

title: G03. Classical-quality parameters for quantum-proof Raz extraction
open: Match classical entropy, output, and error parameters for quantum-proof Raz extraction in product or exact-Markov models.
status: Quantum security and quasilinear implementation are established in 2025, but parameter penalties remain; lossless improvements for a different extractor do not settle Raz’s construction.
why: Raz’s asymmetric entropy requirements make it useful when sources have very different quality.
key_works: Foreman–Wooltorton–Milner–Curchod (2025), [*An efficient construction of Raz’s two-source randomness extractor with improved parameters*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.15547); Miller–Sandfuchs–Ferradini (2025), [*Improved Two-source Extractors against Quantum Side Information*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05528).

title: G04. Extraction with approximately Markov quantum side information
open: When \(I(X:Y\mid E)\le\delta\), determine whether exact-Markov-secure extraction incurs only a dimension-independent additional error \(f(\delta)\to0\), or construct a counterexample.
status: Explicitly raised in 2016. Approximate recoverability does not automatically reproduce exact conditional-independence structure.
why: Physical sources rarely satisfy exact mathematical independence.
key_works: Arnon-Friedman–Portmann–Scholz (2016), [*Quantum-proof multi-source randomness extractors in the Markov model*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.TQC.2016.2), [arXiv:1510.06743](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.06743).

title: G05. Sublinear-entropy extraction from two independent processes
open: Extract from two independent channels acting on arbitrarily correlated, possibly entangled inputs when each channel supplies only sublinear fresh conditional min-entropy.
status: The 2025/2026 independent-process framework gives inner-product constructions above a high entropy-sum threshold, tight for inner product itself.
why: Independent physical processes need not produce independent classical outputs.
key_works: Sandfuchs–Ferradini–Renner (2025/2026), [*Randomness from causally independent processes*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05203).

title: G06. Generic lifting to causally independent processes
open: Transform arbitrary classical two-source extractors into extractors for independent processes with controlled entropy/error loss, or identify necessary additional conditions through counterexamples.
status: Explicitly posed in 2025; exact-Markov lifting does not cover independent channels acting on correlated inputs.
why: Would make a large classical construction toolkit applicable to broader physical source models.
key_works: Sandfuchs–Ferradini–Renner (2025/2026), [*Randomness from causally independent processes*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05203).

title: G07. Seedless device-independent extraction with memoryful devices
open: Secure deterministic privacy amplification from Bell-certified data when devices retain quantum memory and adapt measurements to prior inputs and outputs, retaining positive rate.
status: Seedless extraction and the asymptotic one-key-bit-per-singlet one-party rate are established for memoryless measurements; memoryful devices remain open.
why: Device memory is a natural adversarial capability in repeated experiments.
key_works: Foreman–Masanes (2025), [*Seedless extractors for device-independent quantum cryptography*](https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2025-03-06-1654); Lin–Foreman–Masanes (2026), [*High-rate and computationally-efficient seedless extractors for device-independent quantum cryptography*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.31525).

title: G08. Explicit matrices for high-rate seedless device-independent extraction
open: Efficiently construct binary matrices satisfying the required row-space weight conditions across the full block-length and rate range of the high-rate theorem.
status: The 2026 revision proves existence and efficient evaluation given a suitable matrix; BCH candidates do not achieve all claimed parameters.
why: An existential matrix does not supply an implementable extractor at every operating point.
key_works: Lin–Foreman–Masanes (2026), [*High-rate and computationally-efficient seedless extractors for device-independent quantum cryptography*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.31525).

title: G09. Quantum nonmalleable extraction with optimal seed and entropy
open: Achieve \(d=O(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\), \(k=O(\log\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon))\), and output \(\Omega(k)\) against quantum side information and admissible seed tampering.
status: Classical constructions reach this target; checked quantum constructions retain polylogarithmic seed and entropy requirements.
why: Would make active quantum privacy amplification nearly entropy optimal.
key_works: Boddu–Jain–Kapshikar (2021/2024), [*Quantum secure non-malleable-extractors*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.03097); Li (2023), [*Two Source Extractors for Asymptotically Optimal Entropy, and (Many) More*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.06802).

title: G10. Two-round quantum privacy amplification with optimal loss
open: From \(H_{\min}(X\mid E)\ge k\), obtain efficient two-round active privacy amplification outputting \(k-O(\log\log n+s)\) bits with error \(2^{-s}\) for \(s\le ck\).
status: Quantum two-round feasibility is established, but checked constructions retain roughly half the entropy; classical protocols reach the stronger target.
why: Would preserve scarce quantum-secure entropy under an actively attacked communication channel.
